llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Apple jobs lookup helper that sends user-directed requests to Crawlora and does not show hidden, persistent, destructive, or deceptive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a Crawlora API key and outbound HTTPS requests to a third-party API, which is disclosed and proportionate to its function; users should expect search terms and job IDs to be sent to Crawlora.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency installation, remote code retrieval, or package mutation behavior was found in the artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The helper limits destination and path, but it still accepts POST bodies even though the documented Apple Jobs endpoints are GET-only; this is a hardening gap rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No sudo, root escalation, background worker, scheduled task, memory writing, or persistent modification was found; the temporary curl config is chmod 600 and removed on exit.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to search public Apple Careers postings and fetch job details; the helper implements that through a fixed Crawlora API base URL and two allowlisted Apple Jobs paths.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable using Crawlora as a third-party service for Apple jobs research. Keep CRAWLORA_API_KEY private, avoid sending sensitive text as query or body content, and prefer normal GET calls shown in the skill documentation.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: The lack of explicit allowed-tools or permissions metadata is a packaging hardening gap, but the artifact instructions and helper are narrow and do not request broad unrelated authority.
[E1] expected: External transmission is expected for this API-backed skill and is disclosed in SKILL.md; the destination is fixed to Crawlora rather than attacker-controlled.
[PE2] expected: The cited chmod 600 operation protects the temporary curl config file and is not sudo or root execution.
[SQP-2] expected: The endpoint reference mentions the API key and third-party endpoint; SKILL.md also tells users not to hardcode, query-param, or commit the key.
[T09] unexpected: The POST/body capability exceeds the documented GET-only endpoint contract, but it remains limited to the fixed Crawlora host and two Apple Jobs routes and does not enable arbitrary file upload or credential redirection.
